body:
> The next one is scheduled for October 2, 9AM PDT

I'm assuming this is actually October 9, 9AM PDT - can you confirm @cwilso?

I marked https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10673 to check in again on getting CSS Modules to Stage 2 if @smaug---- has had a chance to investigate.

# Minutes:

2025-10-09 (AMER + EMEA)
Tracking issue: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11747 

## Attendees
[Noam Rosenthal](mailto:nrosenthal@google.com) [smaug@mozilla.com](mailto:smaug@mozilla.com) [Dominic Farolino](mailto:domfarolino@google.com) [Mason Freed](mailto:masonfreed@google.com) Jacques Newman, [kschmi@microsoft.com](mailto:kschmi@microsoft.com) [keithamus@gmail.com](mailto:keithamus@gmail.com) [zcorpan@mozilla.com](mailto:zcorpan@mozilla.com) [lwarlow@igalia.com](mailto:lwarlow@igalia.com) [Robert Flack](mailto:flackr@google.com) [Joey Arhar](mailto:jarhar@google.com) [Kagami Rosylight](mailto:krosylight@mozilla.com) [stephanie.zhang@microsoft.com](mailto:stephanie.zhang@microsoft.com) [annevk@annevk.nl](mailto:annevk@annevk.nl) [Jan-Niklas Jäschke](mailto:jjaschke@mozilla.com) [Lea Verou](mailto:lea@verou.me) [David Baron](mailto:dbaron@dbaron.org) 

## Agenda
### Review past action items
Meeting time poll (Chris) - carry over to next meeting, as Chris won’t attend this one.
[zcorpan] write clear commit message for [Redact ancestorOrigins using referrer policy](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11560#discussion_r2338608768) so that we can ping the right people

### Carryovers
[Out of order HTML streaming ("patching") · Issue #11542 · whatwg/html](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542) noam/foolip
[WHATUP at TPAC 2025: agenda suggestions · Issue #11711 · whatwg/html](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11711) cwilso
[Menu elements proposal · Issue #11729 · whatwg/html](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11729) domfarolino, “discuss this at the WHATNOT meeting scheduled for 2025-10-09”

### New topics
Requesting stage 2 for [XSLT](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11523). PRs: [HTML](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11563)/[DOM](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1400). Relevant: [”risky changes” guidelines](https://whatwg.org/working-mode#risky-changes).
Requesting stage 2 for [[focusgroup] Declarative keyboard focus navigation for a scoped set of composite widgets](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11641#top) https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11641 . [Jacques Newman]
Requesting stage 2 for [FormControlRange Interface #11478](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11478)
[Declarative CSS Modules and Declarative Shadow DOM adoptedstylesheets attribute](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10673#top) https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10673 
Expose certain behavioural attributes via ElementInternals https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11752
Minutes
Topic: carryover

Noam: carryover action items. Meeting time poll is deferred.

Anne: I think Simon’s action item is done.

Noam: I’ll take an action item to get the ancestorOrigins PR reviewed from Google’s perspective.

Topic: Out-of-order HTML streaming (patching)

Noam: Lots of feedback on HTML streaming and the HTML tree manipulation methods. [Missed a bit on Trusted Types.] Proposal is to have a template element with a contentfor attribute that points to an element with a matching contentname attribute. Then the template element contents will be streamed into that element. For further details see https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542

Anne: worried about the increasing overloading of the <template> element. Too many jobs. Otherwise, I like how the first part works - fairly simple. Slight improvement to not use an id attribute, to avoid XSS, opt-in on both ends.

Simon: feedback from Jake that declarative solution might not be good enough for real world scenarios.

Noam: some of that feedback resulted in additional proposals, such as the contentrevision attribute. Would be good to hear from Jake directly, but we did attempt to address all his feedback. Also got a lot of good feedback from framework authors and others.

Simon: once we have the API, could you polyfill this?

Noam: yup.

Robert Flack: can you have multiple streams?

Noam: with some restrictions.

Robert Flack: do we have a path for more complicated scenarios where streaming and server connection management intersect?

Noam: I think so.

Noam: we’ll work on a PR that explains more of the details.

Topic: TPAC

Noam: I’ll let Chris handle this next week.

Anne: if you want something discussed at TPAC, better add it to the issue now.

Topic: Menu elements proposal

[https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11729 was explained by Dominic.]

Dominic: everyone please take a look, we’d like to get to stage 1.

Anne: curious about the scope as historically these proposals were always about influencing “native UI”.

Dominic: that’s not the goal.

Dominic: I’d love to go for stage 1.

Anne: I’d like a week if that’s okay.

Olli: I’d like two weeks.

Topic: Deprecating XSLT

Mason: I’d like to go for stage 2.

Mason: I went through the websites that could be broken and most could be fixed with the polyfill or extension. Still have to figure out the WPT situation.

Mason: Wanted to discuss the risky changes section as to whether others wanted to ship at the same time.

Anne: supportive, but not prepared to lead. Would take a patch for a console warning.

Simon: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1990759

[Mozilla was also supportive.]

Mason: would appreciate more review.

Topic: focusgroup

Jacques: would like stage 2 for https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11641. 

Olli: the amount of detail is somewhat lacking. E.g., how does directional navigation really work? Also, how this interact with reading flow? I’m worried that focus management will get quite complex.

Anne: I think it should integrate better with the existing focus model, e.g., focusable areas. Make it clear how it works as part of the existing focus management model. That’s probably a pre-requisite for stage 2.

Topic: declarative CSS modules

Anne: are we going to regret defining this as data: URLs? Does this require implementations to implement it as such?

[Unclear.]

Kurt: I’ll come back in two weeks to ask for stage 2 again and will try to address that question meanwhile. Also would appreciate review.

Noam: I’ll also take a look.

Topic: Expose certain behavioural attributes via ElementInternals

Luke: [Gives an exposition.]

[People seem generally interested.]

Topic: FormControlRange

Noam: sorry we ended up skipping this. We’ll do it next time.
